newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* Deng Xiaoping, a founding revolutionary of Communist China and the architect of modern China's economic reforms, died at 92 of respiratory failure after suffering from Parkinson's disease.

* News Analysis: Deng's successors face potentially divisive challenges, including pressure for greater economic liberalisation, greater scrutiny of human rights, corruption and the balance of relations with Taiwan and Hong Kong.

* U.S. officials briefed Mexico's anti-drug chief on sensitive information regarding their anti-narcotics operations in Mexico just days before the Mexican government detained him on charges of collaborating with drug traffickers.
* The U.S. government says it sees few drastic changes in how it will handle its diplomatic relations with China after the death of China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping.
* The Supreme Court upheld a ruling requiring protestors at abortion clinics to stay at least 15 feet away from clinic doorways and driveways.

* Deng's anointed successor, Jiang Zemin, is a quiet intellectual who favours steady economic liberalisation and likes to quote from the Gettysburg address. He appears to be a secure strongman, but tends to shift with the political winds and has been associated more with caution than with leadership.
